resources.string: Your own exit on ordinary hosting

Experimental mode. Traffic goes not through VLESS servers but through your own exit: the OpenFlux app (Node.js) on ordinary web hosting. Useful when your mobile carrier only lets \"whitelisted\" sites through and your hosting is one of them. TCP only (ports 80/443), speed is modest.
Traffic goes through your exit instead of VLESS servers
First set up the connection to the exit (address and token, or the channel link), then save.
The address must start with http:// or https://
The address must point to a .php file (e.g. …/phpbox.php)
Without HTTPS your provider can see the token and the site addresses. The content of HTTPS sites stays encrypted.
The VPN is connected: exit settings changes apply on reconnect.
How to set up your own exit
1. Get the Node.js exit (app.js) from the openflux-exit branch (button below) — it also has a step-by-step Beget guide.
2. Put your own long random token into config.json.
3. Run it on the host via Passenger (Node.js) — see the guide.
4. Paste the exit address and the token here.

Traffic goes through a document in Mail.ru Cloud. Helps when the carrier only lets whitelisted sites through. The channel is not encrypted (HTTPS sites stay encrypted) and is slower than direct.
Traffic goes through cups.online rooms. Helps when the carrier only lets whitelisted sites through. The channel is not encrypted (HTTPS sites stay encrypted) and is slower than direct.
Connect to any OpenFlux node by an openflux://… link (your VPS, a friend\'s node). The channel is encrypted when the link or the field below has a key.
The demo server always works directly; the channel applies to your own exit only.
